audit_question: Why did the regime detector report trending_up during a broad selloff (SPY -1.52%)?

regime_timeline.note: Session start — inherited from prior smoothed state
CORRECT flip — detected sell-off ~50 min into session
INCORRECT flip back — market still selling (SPY ~-1.0% at this point)
INCORRECT flip back within 26 seconds — then STAYS trending_up until close

regime_duration_summary.market_actual: SPY -1.52% — should have been trending_down for majority of session

sma_lookback.effect: 200-minute (~3.3 hours) lookback means the SMA incorporates prior-day and early-session uptrend data. On a day that opens down, the SMA slope can still be positive because it includes yesterday's late rally.
sma_lookback.severity: HIGH — this is the primary contributor

trend_slope_window.effect: Only 10 minutes of SMA change is used for slope calculation. During choppy sell-offs with brief bounces, 10 bars can briefly show positive slope even as the market trends lower.

ema_smoothing.effect: After the session opened with trending_up (inherited from 3/11 close), the smoothed trending_up probability stayed elevated. When trending_down briefly appeared at 10:20, the smoothed probs shifted toward trending_down. But after a small bounce around 12:30, the raw scores briefly favored trending_up, and the EMA snapped back. The 0.7 persistence factor then kept trending_up dominant for the rest of the session.

threshold_scaling.effect: Extremely small threshold means even tiny positive SMA slopes trigger trending_up. A 0.1% upward slope in the SMA (which can persist for hours after a prior-day rally) is enough.

cross_session_contamination.finding: Smoothed probabilities persist across sessions via brain state. The 3/11 close was trending_up. On 3/12 open, the smoothed_probs['trending_up'] was already high (~0.6-0.8) before any new bars were processed.
cross_session_contamination.severity: HIGH — prior-day regime dominates early-session detection

whether_inverse_etf_logic_was_effectivel.answer: PARTIALLY — but the primary blocker was confidence, not regime
detail: SH appeared as a candidate 8 times, always with eff_conf=0.00
PSQ appeared as a candidate 3 times, always with eff_conf=0.00
During trending_down windows (15:20-17:37), SH/PSQ WERE produced but with zero confidence
The regime flip logic in alpha_scanner._regime_alignment() correctly flips trending_down→trending_up for SH/PSQ — this gives them positive regime alignment (5% weight)
But regime alignment is only 5% of the alpha score. With breakout_readiness=0 and squeeze_momentum=0, the overall alpha score is near-zero regardless of regime
CONCLUSION: Even with a perfect regime detector, SH/PSQ would still have eff_conf=0.00 because the confidence formula is 0.65*breakout + 0.35*tension, and both components are zero for inverse ETFs

exact_suspect_files_lines.issue: SMA(200) on 1-min bars is too laggy for intraday regime detection
10-bar slope window is too short to distinguish trend from noise
EMA alpha=0.3 preserves prior regime too strongly
Smoothed state persists across sessions — contaminates next-day open

would_correct_detector_have_called_trend.answer: YES — a correctly functioning detector should have reported trending_down for ~80% of the session (after 10:00 ET). SPY fell -1.52% in a steady decline with no meaningful reversal.
would_correct_detector_have_called_trend.caveat: The regime DID correctly detect trending_down from 10:20-12:37 ET (the strongest selling window). It failed to maintain that call as selling decelerated in the afternoon.

recommended_investigation: Consider separate intraday SMA period (e.g., 50 instead of 200 on 1-min bars)
Consider resetting smoothed_probs at session open instead of carrying forward
Consider using returns-based trend detection instead of SMA slope
Consider adding SPY intraday-return-from-open as a direct regime input
